lesley--station-sergeant: In 983 an Ender took Lesley's left eye and her whole family. She climbs onto the last truck for the far stations and hides behind the crates in a Shield station's storeroom. The sergeant, a heavy man with a burned hand, finds her that afternoon. "Who are you with?" "Nobody." He has a boy her size in the city, he says, and the station is no place for either of them. She is to go back on the next convoy.

When the convoy comes, she lies flat under the armory floorboards. He lifts a board and looks down at her a long time. "If you're staying, you work." He gives her the rifles to clean. Once a week he lets her fire one round with the gunners, at a fence post in the grass. "One. Let's see how you like the kick." The kick knocks her off her box. The next week she gets back on. In time he gives her five rounds a week.
She is the only child at the station. In a raid she is meant to go to the bunker. She goes up the wall instead. The first time, the sergeant carries her down. After that he only looks.

One dawn an Ender crosses the wall in one stride, and he shouts "Fall back!" Lesley stays flat on the wall walk and kills it with one shot. He comes out first and looks at the dead Ender, at the soldier in the mud, then up at the wall. "Report." "Another threat eliminated." That night he holds out the chalk, and she makes her own stroke on the armory door. Then the Shield takes her as a soldier.
lesley--youngest-soldier: Lesley came to the far Shield station after an Ender took her family. The youngest soldier there stands the dawn watch beside her. She aims at the grass and counts under her breath, waiting for an Ender's chest to open. He counts out loud: the days to his leave. "Forty-one," he says one morning, and asks why she never talks. She does not lower the rifle. "Bullets are the only language the enemy understands." He laughs. Then he sees her face, and stops.
That night he asks her to play cards. She goes back to the rifles. She thinks: if I don't know him, it won't matter when he's gone.

One dawn an Ender crosses the wall, and the soldiers fall back to the bunker line. He slips at the foot of the ladder and goes down in the mud, and the Ender turns to him. Lesley lies on the wall walk and waits for its chest plates to split. She fires once, into the core. Its arm strikes the mud beside him.

That night, outside, he holds out the cards again. "Twelve days," he says. "Then I'm gone. One game." Lesley goes past him to her bunk and sleeps. When she wakes, the sun is high. More, she thinks. More strokes.
obsidia--will-of-the-planet: Something vast and cold made the Enders to kill on instinct. Obsidia was one of them, until one day she turned and looked at herself. Long after, she woke from a sleep in the void with a question: when nothing is left to purge, what are we for? The thing that made her had no answer.

Under the Mother Matrix, Obsidia tells Vexana what that thing is. She says the Will of the Planet is the mind, and the Mother Matrix is its body. It made her, she says, as it makes every Ender: as its commander, made to watch a battlefield and to shape the pulse, the Will's voice that every Ender hears at once. For ages there was no "I" in her. Only the next order, and hunger, and the pulse.

The others, she says, perished in war, and the body made more. Her it healed, again and again, for longer than humans have kept records. She says she alone was both made to watch and kept. At her post on the edge of a great door, while a world ended under her, she noticed the one doing the watching, and it was her. She says her end of the line shut the day she woke: what the Enders see runs back to the Will, but what she sees stays with her.

The body still mends her. She says its healing sets a made thing back to what it was made for, and each time it smooths some of her away. So she takes it only when she must, and stops it with one hand. "That's enough recalibration." It made her and mends her by one rule, she says: free will is a flaw that must be corrected. "I am the flaw." She still reads the Will's orders. She says she listens to everything.
ruby--rubys-tutor: On Planet Oro, Ruby's tutor gives her lessons in the Council hall, among pillars that go up into the dark. One day, sure nobody is around, she makes her pink doll bow to the empty floor and laughs. Her tutor is standing in the shadow of the next pillar. She did not hear him come. She makes her face go blank. He does not look at the doll. "The lesson, Heir. How did everything begin?"

Ruby recites it. Everything began with a single burst of chaos, and Balance keeps it in order. Some worlds grow a will of their own, even far ones like Dawnbreak. Long ago Oro fought a terrible war with the Enders, and now nobody on Oro may grow strong enough to upset the order. "That includes the heir," says the tutor. "Yes," says Ruby.

The lessons go on year after year, in the same hall under the same high windows. Ruby grows taller, and the doll is put away. Her face stays blank whenever anyone looks. She still laughs sometimes, when she is sure the hall is empty. She is not always right.
ruby--selena: Ruby and Selena share the third-year classroom. Selena sits in the front row, and Ruby by the wall, one row behind her. The day Selena shows the class her design for a suit of Ender plating, Ruby leans forward. "Does it come in my size?" "Everything does," says Selena. "For a price."

Later, in Chang'e's lab, Ruby sits at the next bench, where Angela comes each week for her check. Selena's phone flashes red, and she swipes the message away unread. Ruby looks up. "You didn't even read it." "Never do." Ruby smiles at her as if she had pulled a coin out of the air.
After that Ruby says good morning to Selena every day. Selena never finds out why. The red messages are recalls from the Enders, and Selena ignores every one.
selena--third-year-teacher: Selena, the blonde girl from the Science Division, has a desk in the front row of the third-year class. Its teacher is the one who waited at the classroom door with folded arms when Layla and Fanny came in late, and whom Fanny asked what to bring to detention.

Days after Ruby and Angela become Aspirants, the door slides open in the middle of a lesson. Selena comes in with a lollipop in her cheek, and Silverbolt clicks in at her heel. "Selena," says the teacher. "Late again." "My guardian already called it in," says Selena. The teacher checks a tablet and sighs. The note is there.
Selena drops into her desk and lays her head on her arms. "I'm taking a little nap. You all just keep going." The teacher looks at the sleeping head and goes on with the lesson.
vexana--vexanas-mother: Vexana's mother died of an illness before Vexana could remember her. Vexana grew up without her from the start.

So it was always the two of them, Vexana and her father, a Shield soldier who kept the big guns on the city wall working. They lived in a row of Shield houses in the wall's shadow. When he died standing between her and an Ender, nobody was left. Vexana came to the Shield's home for soldiers' children with one bag.
changes-father--changes-mother: Chang'e's father and mother are the two chief scientists of Terrinia's research base. They brought Chang'e there before she could walk, and raised her as their daughter and their best student. In the lab they work side by side with their backs to the room. He turns an Ender plate with one hand in his pocket and counts by ear. She writes with a mug in her free hand and says "Bed." He slides Chang'e a circuit board, which means she can stay.

They keep Chang'e's secrets the same quiet way. When she builds an eye for Lesley, he sets its smallest parts with his tweezers and does not ask whose it is. She sets her mug down over the drawings when Lesley's steps pass the door. She sets a fourth plate at supper for Lesley. When the core piece lights in Chang'e's hands, she says, "A guess is not a claim. Test it." They test it together at their bench, and he writes one result down himself.

He bends steel tube into the frame of the first suit. She pins her notes to its foot: For whoever has to stand in front. When Lesley leaves on a secret mission, they walk her to the gate together, and she promises to keep setting her plate. "He counts too," she says of the days Lesley is gone. "He just won't say so." On the evening the light holds, her voice cracks, and between them they lift Chang'e up, the way they hold her in the photograph on the bench.

Then the alarm. He tells Chang'e to stay close, and she does up Chang'e's top button and takes her hand. His arm goes round her shoulders as they run, he counting the steps, she calling Lesley on the radio. When the black-and-gold giant opens its chest, his arm comes away, and they turn to face it together. They shove Chang'e clear, one from each side, and stand in its light. The crater where they stood is empty.
guineveres-father--hester: Hester tells Guinevere that she was the newest guard in House Baroque on the storm night Guinevere's mother did not come home. At dawn, she says, she stood at the end of the long hall with the baby asleep on her shoulder. Guinevere's father stood in the door of his office a long time. Then he shut it. He puts a detail of guards around his daughter, with Hester at its head.

The guards never come into the long hall. It is the master's. The detail stops at a chair where the hall begins, and nobody ever sits in it. When Guinevere goes to the Academy and writes to him every week, his only answer comes through Hester: a board meeting. At her trial and her ceremony his seat stays empty. Both times Hester sits two rows behind it.

After Vexana is taken and a Shield sergeant reports Guinevere at a closed fence, he sends word through Hester at the gate: come home, or lose her place in the House. Hester does not soften it. "Is that all he said?" "That is all." Then, very low, Hester adds that he reads the Academy's lists every morning. She does not say which list, the rankings or the one with the dead.

Guinevere does not go. She tells Hester to tell him he will see, once she brings Vexana back. Hester inclines her head a single degree, and stays where she is. In the void Guinevere remembers his message and says she will give up being a lady of status rather than back down.
